clue.text: Chain of events making poor cat once lead the race

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so the jumbled words come before the next piece
something in poor shape is out of order, so the following words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a race or people is a nation

explanation.surface: A sorry old cat once led the field, setting off a chain of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A concatenation is a linked series, so a chain of events is a concatenation of them.

clue.text: Egg-carrying four, so I've found out

indicators.note: found out suggests letters dug out and laid down differently, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naturalist discovering that four creatures are carrying eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviferous is the biological term for bearing or carrying eggs, from Latin ovum.

clue.text: English dean on the French in bed

indicators.note: one word lying in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
le is a French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: An English cleric lying in bed with a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: John Colet was the Tudor dean of St Paul's and founder of St Paul's School.
explanation.definitionFit: John Colet, humanist scholar, served as dean of St Paul's Cathedral in London.

clue.text: Genus of molluscs start trilling chorus wildly

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of trilling

indicators.note: something going wildly is out of control, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shellfish breaking into a wild trilling song.
explanation.definitionFit: Trochus is a genus of top-shell sea snails, which are gastropod molluscs.

clue.text: Short year for Greek governor?

parts.note: surface reading: a year cut short in length
setter's reading: a year short of one month, the one lacking the third month of spring

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'no March' and it describes a year missing a month; whole, it is a Greek official. The question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomarch is the governor of a nome, an administrative province of modern or ancient Greece and Egypt.

clue.text: Exciting literary critic going in head first

indicators.note: the critic's name has something going into it, enclosing that letter

parts.note: Lionel Trilling was a leading American literary critic

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the opening letter of head

explanation.surface: A literary critic diving in head first sounds thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Lionel Trilling (1905-75) wrote The Liberal Imagination; the H slips in after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling and exciting are synonyms describing something that gives a rush of excitement.

clue.text: Nothing to scrutinise in ancient Italic language

parts.note: O resembles zero, nothing
to scan is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A scholar finding nothing to examine in an old Italian tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was an Indo-European language of southern Italy, related to Latin and now extinct.

clue.text: Setting up in business

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the act of founding something
second meaning: a firm, shop or institution

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about starting a company, but splits into the act of founding and the thing founded.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the founding of something and an organisation such as a shop or hotel.

clue.text: Reward for deliberation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a payment or recompense

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like payment for thinking something over; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fee or recompense paid and the act of careful thought.

clue.text: Not yet full pantry?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: there is ..., read as a phrase
second meaning: a room for storing preserves and food

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read two ways: the phrase 'still room' (space left over) and the household word for a storeroom. The question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A still-room was originally where cordials were distilled, later the storeroom of a large house, much like a pantry.

clue.text: Take to part of book

parts.note: REC is short for recipe, Latin for 'take', heading old prescriptions
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry something over to a section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front of each leaf.

clue.text: One who acts as a little gentleman

parts.note: taken as written
gent is the shortened form of gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone who plays the part of a small gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' asks for the clipped word, not a small man.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is a person who acts on behalf of another, or simply a doer.

clue.text: Bad luck an actor can't remember, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British-style exclamation of sympathy for misfortune
second meaning: lines of script that are difficult to learn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines!' is an old British and Australian way of saying 'bad luck!'; read literally it is difficult dialogue for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom commiserating with misfortune, and literally describes difficult script passages.

clue.text: Charge less to go round for animal

indicators.note: one word going round another surrounds it, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Reads like a vet or zoo deciding to charge less for an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a price, but it is the electrical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, a large wild animal.

clue.text: Referring to outer covering of primed ice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of the outer coating of specially prepared ice.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the anagram: the odd phrase 'primed ice' is itself the hint that its letters need rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermic means relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of skin or tissue.

clue.text: Lifted broken ties in coal-scuttle

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits inside the next item

parts.note: a hod is a coal scuttle

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lifted a coal scuttle that had broken ties in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise up, so hoisted is a past-tense synonym of lifted.

clue.text: Tickle one drawer in art gallery

indicators.note: items placed in something are enclosed by it

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
I is the Roman numeral for one
a till is a cash drawer

explanation.surface: An artist amusing visitors at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' wants to be an artist, but it is the cash drawer of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to stimulate or excite pleasantly, the figurative sense of tickle.

clue.text: Inactive in south-eastern isles, possibly

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the word before it is reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone or something lying idle on a group of islands in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Sessile describes organisms fixed in one place and not moving freely, hence sedentary or inactive.

clue.text: Point to one bit of vulcanised rubber?

parts.note: E is the compass point east

indicators.note: vulcanised material has been treated and changed in structure, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone indicating a single piece of hardened rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulcanised rubber' reads as one material, but 'vulcanised' is the signal and 'rubber' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebonite is a hard black form of rubber made by vulcanising it with much sulphur.

clue.text: Means of ignition in a ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device for lighting cigarettes or fires
second meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for loading and unloading vessels

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like something that starts a fire aboard ship; the second sense is a barge used in harbours.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small flame-producing gadget and a cargo barge that ferries goods to ships.

clue.text: Row one has for example over ancestry

parts.note: a row is a line
a means one

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A family argument with someone holding forth over their family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is line of descent from ancestors, the same as ancestry.

clue.text: Animal: one to go after with old fire-arm?-

parts.note: a musket is also a male sparrowhawk
the setter uses the ring-shaped letter for one, a loose equivalence
on means after or further, as in 'from then on'

explanation.surface: Suggests a hunter pursuing an animal with an antique gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: a musket is a male sparrowhawk, followed by O for one and ON for after. The trailing dash is a print blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A musketoon was a short, large-bore musket of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Apply oneself to argument

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to start working in earnest
second meaning: a fight or squabble

explanation.walkthrough: As a verb phrase it means get down to work; as a noun it is a scrap or quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To 'set to' is to begin work vigorously, and a set-to is a brief fight or quarrel.

clue.text: Share out a tax-return

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a toll is a levy or tax

explanation.surface: Splitting up a tax refund between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax-return' looks like a single form; the hyphen hides a word and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or assign portions, which is sharing out.

clue.text: Back jester to have article withdrawn

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a fool was a court jester

explanation.surface: Supporting a jester whose item is pulled from the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' looks like part of the story about an article being pulled; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and reserved in manner, the same as withdrawn.

clue.text: Part of insect thorax making unusual mount

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the word's letters come out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An entomologist preparing an odd specimen mount from an insect's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The notum is the dorsal plate of each segment of an insect's thorax.

clue.text: He is in love with a motor in a way

indicators.note: in a different way means arranged otherwise, so the words before are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man infatuated with his car, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as one phrase; the anagram uses 'in a' as letters and 'way' alone as its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover, a man who is enamoured of someone.

clue.text: Firm tender of interest to builder

parts.note: surface reading: a definite bid for a contract
setter's reading: the word for firm is also the building material, which a builder cares about

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' doubles as the adjective that also names a building material poured on site, which is why a builder would take interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a bid to do a job, and a concrete one is definite and binding.
